knowledge_type_note: Official rule (A). The commonly used 'insufficient material' shortcut is an implementation convention, not the FIDE rule, and is classified separately.
definition_short: A position from which neither player can checkmate by ANY series of legal moves. The game is drawn immediately.
definition_long:
FIDE Art. 5.2.2: 'The game is drawn when a position has arisen in which neither player can checkmate the opponent's king with any series of legal moves. The game is said to end in a dead position. This immediately ends the game...'

This is broader and stricter than the 'insufficient material' test most software implements. 'Insufficient material' asks whether the material present could ever mate; a dead position asks whether mate is reachable from THIS position by any legal continuation, which includes blocked positions with plenty of material. Conversely, K+B vs K+B on the same colour is insufficient in the FIDE sense, whereas K+N vs K+N is NOT automatically dead, because a helpmate exists.

Nox Chess should not conflate the two terms when explaining a draw.

preconditions: No sequence of legal moves from this position ends in checkmate
indicators_for: K+B vs K+B with bishops on the same colour
indicators_against: Any pawn remains on the board
A rook or queen remains on the board
K+N+N vs K — mate is not forcible but is not impossible, so the position is not dead

exceptions: K+N+N vs K is a draw in practice but is NOT a dead position: mate is legally reachable with cooperation, so the game does not end automatically.
A completely blocked position with full material can be a dead position even though material is ample.
limitations: Deciding the general case is hard; engines and servers approximate it with a material test. The approximation is correct in the common cases and wrong at the edges.

examples.note: King and bishop against king. FIDE 5.2.2 calls a position dead when no series of legal moves can lead to checkmate, and this is the textbook instance: with one bishop there is no mating net at all, whatever either side plays. The move generator confirms the position is live in the ordinary sense - 11 legal moves, no check - which is the point: dead-position is not about having no moves, it is about no sequence of moves reaching mate. That is why it is the one official rule in this base whose detectability is recorded as heuristic rather than mechanical.

tablebase.note: PROVEN draw over every legal continuation, which is the strongest form the claim can take: FIDE 5.2.2 says no series of legal moves can lead to checkmate, and a tablebase is a statement about every series of legal moves. This is one of the few places in this base where the evidence and the definition are the same shape.

by_level.beginner: Neither side has enough left to deliver checkmate, so the game is a draw.
by_level.intermediate: Dead position: no legal sequence of moves from here could ever produce checkmate, so the game ends drawn at once.
by_level.advanced: Art. 5.2.2. Note this is broader than the 'insufficient material' test implemented by most software.

avoid: insufficient material (when the FIDE rule is meant)
